pr_body:
sets sensor value to None and sets available attr when sensor missing



## Proposed change
Handle Errors processing temp data from venstar api.
When a remote sensor is offline or otherwise unavailable,  the api simply does not return that section.
When we load the value from the return dict,  we end up with a None, which errors when trying to parse as a float.
This PR both handles that error, and sets the entity to unavailable.  
It also returns the sensor to available if the value is returned later.

issue_context.title: Venstar Integration fails when remote sensor offline
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The venstar module fails to update when a previously available sensor is no longer present in the api.  Because of the way the api (and upstream library) handle remote sensors which are offline,  It is possible for calls to `get_sensor` to return None, rather than a valid value.  Because the call to `get_sensor` occurs in a lambda wrapped with math,  a response of None cannot be processed and results in a traceback (See Below).



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.8.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Venstar

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/venstar/

_No response_

_No response_

I would like to throw my hat in the ring for this as well. When one of my ACC-TSENWIFIPRO remote sensors go offline, the integration flatlines and records what the last temperature value was, despite the ColorTouch 7850 throwing a warning/error.

can you open `http://<your_thermostat_ip>/query/sensors` in a browser when the remote sensor is present and when it is missing and post both here? 
I'm not sure how the thermostat will change the output when it is missing and how it shows up as missing with determine how a fix is made.

hmm, the JSON you posted seems like the `UPBEDROOM1` sensor is no different than the `MASTBEDSENSOR`.

From that output, I don't see why hass would have an issue with the sensor missing.

I've been dropping tickets via email to thermostatsupport@venstar.com and getting prompt responses. Although, the responses aren't ideal.

I've uncovered several bugs with the ACCTSENWIFI devices that are apparently being phased out per one of their responses.

1) Mac address in the app is off on the last alphanumeric character compared to the device MAC address in the router
2) These sensors HATE multiple AP's - they frequently drop offline until power cycled
3) There isn't a documented API call to show accuracy/parity between the venstar app/thermostat against the API JSON response..

My latest ticket was for #3 - I would encourage anyone having this issue to ask for the dev team to fix the ColorTouch thermostat API as it relates to remote sensor values when they become offline

Why are you calling here the function again?
If the function has raised a TypeError before, it will raise it here again so catching the TypeError is useless.
Why are you using the coordinator logger and not a logger for this file?
